newsitem.title: FRANCE: UAE seeks Dassault Mirage 2000 upgrades - paper.
newsitem.headline: UAE seeks Dassault Mirage 2000 upgrades - paper.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is negotiating a modernisation of its fleet of Mirage 2000 combat planes, newspaper Le Monde reported on Friday.
The upgrade would bring the Dassault Aviation Mirage 2000, which Abu Dhabi bought in the mid-1980s, up to the level of the new Mirage 2000-9, which the UAE is also currently in talks to buy.
The UAE requirement is for around 20 Mirage 2000-9 multi-role planes, an industrial source close to the Mirage programme said.
A separate source told Reuters earlier this week a high-level UAE delegation was in Paris for sales negotiations for 18 Mirage 2000-9 aircraft.
Le Monde said the UAE wants 18 combat planes and between two and four extra aircraft for training.
The newspaper estimated potential value of the contract at 14 billion francs, excluding the weapons systems.
The Mirage 2000-9 is a derivative of the Mirage 2000-5 air defence and ground strike plane which has been sold to France, Qatar and Taiwan.

The Mirage 2000-9 contract is expected to be signed in the next few weeks once price negotiations have been resolved, an industrial source said. This deal is separate from the UAE's competition for up to 80 advanced combat planes, in which Dassault's Rafale is up against Lockheed Martin's F16.
Besides Dassault, which makes the airframe, other French companies sharing the contract would be state-owned Snecma, which makes the motors, and Thomson-CSF, which makes the radar and avionics.

Negotiations are also being held with Matra, a subsidiary of the Lagardere conglomerate, for the sale of its Mica and Magic missiles. The Mirage 2000-9 will also be able to deliver the Apache cruise missile when it enters service.
